q1_issues.issue: The loser is the intransitive subject of "lost" and undergoes no change of state, so the subject test yields Agent (the section's explicit default when unclear), not Patient.
"to Democrat Robb" names the opponent and answers no where/whither question, so the PP-routing rule prescribes the preposition-named oblique (To sk_lose_1 robb) rather than the spatial Goal.

q2_gaps: capitalized role / party appositive noun immediately before a proper name ("Incumbent George Allen", "Democrat Robb") — the mechanical casing cue in *Names and casing* says a capitalized modifier joins the capitalized run (giving democrat_robb), while the appositive rule wants a separate typing atom; nothing adjudicates, and sentence-initial capitalization is not distinguished

ordinal modifier on a noun that has no associated event and no "-est" dimension ("a third term") — the Ordinal scale slot is specified only as "the associated event, or an explicit -est dimension", so the filler used here (the entity's own kind, term) is unlicensed by the spec
notes: Both appositive typings correctly take the past host clause's wrapper, and (But sk_run_1 sk_lose_1) follows the main-clause-first / surface-order rule. The "for a third term" oblique is right under the ground-or-prize branch of the Beneficiary vs (For …) split.
